standard.title: Analyse and evaluate language features and sources
standard.description: analyse and evaluate the ways that language features vary according to the purpose and audience of the text, and the ways that sources and quotations are used in a text
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can analyse how language features are shaped by purpose and audience, and identify how authors use supporting evidence in texts (AC9E7LY03). They have not yet evaluated the effectiveness of language feature choices or the use of sources and quotations — moving from analysis to evaluative judgement.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students analyse and evaluate how language features vary according to purpose and audience, and how sources and quotations are used to support ideas in texts.

nodes.label: Evaluating language features for purpose and audience
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can analyse language feature choices in a text and evaluate whether those choices are effective for the text's purpose and audience — forming and justifying a view.
nodes.minimum_width: Analyse two language features in a text and evaluate whether they are effective for the text's stated purpose and audience, giving reasons for the evaluation.
nodes.typical_width: Analyse and evaluate how language features — including vocabulary, tone, sentence structure and register — vary according to purpose and audience; evaluate an author's language choices and present a reasoned opinion about their effectiveness.
wider: Compare how two different authors addressing the same audience for the same purpose use language features differently, evaluating which approach is more effective and why
Evaluate how language feature choices in a First Nations or culturally specific text are calibrated to their intended community audience — what would be gained or lost for a different audience
Analyse how a text changes when its intended audience changes — taking a formal report and rewriting it for a different audience — and evaluate which version is more effective for each audience

response_modes.reason: Evaluation requires students to apply criteria (effectiveness for purpose and audience) rather than simply describe what they observe. The evaluative move — 'and this is effective/not effective because' — needs to be explicitly scaffolded and practised.

success_criteria: Identifies specific language features in a text and analyses their relationship to the text's purpose and audience.
Evaluates whether the language choices are effective, providing reasoned justification with reference to the text.
nodes.hinge_reason: Node 2 applies the same evaluative move to sources and quotations. The criteria-application scaffold — 'effective for what purpose, for which audience, with what reasoning?' — built at Node 1 is required for Node 2 to produce genuine evaluation rather than impressionistic reaction to source presence or absence.

nodes.label: Evaluating use of sources and quotations
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can evaluate how an author uses sources and quotations in a text — assessing whether sources are used effectively to support ideas — and form and express an opinion about the author's approach.
nodes.minimum_width: Evaluate how one source or quotation is used in a text — explain whether it effectively supports the idea it is meant to substantiate, and give a reasoned opinion about the author's approach.
nodes.typical_width: Evaluate the use of sources and quotations across a text, forming and presenting opinions about how effectively the author has used evidence to support ideas; identify cases where source use is strong and cases where it is weak or misleading.
wider: Investigate how the same source or quotation can be used to support opposing claims depending on what surrounding context and interpretation the author provides
Analyse how sources are selected and framed in a biased text — examining what the author's source choices reveal about their perspective and what sources are absent
Evaluate the source use in a student's own argumentative writing and revise for greater effectiveness

response_modes.reason: Evaluating source use effectively requires students to have encountered a range of approaches — strong integration, weak cherry-picking, selective quotation, absence of sources where sources are needed. Exposure to multiple examples of varying quality builds the comparative benchmark needed for genuine evaluation.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The analysis of how sources can be used to construct rather than discover an argument — including how the same evidence can support opposing conclusions — is sophisticated critical thinking territory with high value for advancing students.
success_criteria: Evaluates whether a source or quotation in a text effectively supports the claim it is used to substantiate.
Forms a clear opinion about the author's use of sources and supports that opinion with reference to the text.
